title: Opus xhigh against Sonnet high planners above the primary rubric's ceiling, both with the combined instruction, judged pairwise

document.name: nlogn
document.title: Integer multiplication below n log n (paper.tex)

task: planning: the argument task only, on E6's extractions F2, F3, F4, F5, F6 and F8 (background accepted)
question: Is Opus xhigh a better planner than Sonnet high above the ceiling, where the primary rubric saturates?
protocol: run from the development session; E11.md on the evidence branch
preregistration: calibration/plans/E11.md (criteria fixed at 00:19 UTC, 2026-10-15, before any run)
comparison: the Sonnet high plans with the combined instruction on the same extractions (E9F2Y, E10F3Y, E9F4Y, E10F5Y, E10F6Y, E9F8Y); control E9F4Y against E10F4Y2; pairwise batch J25

intended.task_prompt: the E8 argument instructions plus the parameters-and-cases sentence (the combined instruction)

J25.value: 14 pairwise verdicts (one Opus judge per order): O favoured on F4 and F8, S on F2 and F5, F3 and F6 tied; sign test 2 of 4, p = 0.69; outcome 'O not shown better'. Control E9F4Y vs E10F4Y2 not tied (net +2; clear on 11 items, slight on 10)

deviations.what: orchestrated by the development session (Opus) with this session's permissions; it only passed prompts and ran exegenius next
three runs launched at 01:07 UTC on a reading later corrected (40% to 45% used); three launched at 01:22 after a permission-classifier denial, on the author's explicit authorisation
the exegenius binary on PATH was rebuilt from master (same code) at 01:17 while three runs were active
F3's sequential second judges (triggered by one S verdict and one tie) were skipped because no outcome row could change

limitations: One paper; one Opus run per extraction.
The control shows run-to-run differences between two Sonnet runs as large as any O-S difference; one run per configuration cannot separate models above the ceiling.
